Sprint Review (page 9), Sprint Retrospective (page 10), Increment (pages 11 and 12), Definition of Done (page 12)

[Beyond the Scrum Guide] = practical steps, examples and the list of effects asked by the learning objectives but not stated in the Guide. [Old wording] = a term from the 2017 Guide that a question may still use.

toc.title: Effects of Skipping the Sprint Retrospective (CSM 1.11)
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1Sprint Review

1.1 Purpose, participants and timebox

Item What the Guide says
Purpose "To inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations"
Who "The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders" and "progress toward the Product Goal is discussed"
What happens The Scrum Team and stakeholders review what was accomplished in the Sprint and what has changed in their environment. Based on this information, attendees collaborate on what to do next
Product Backlog "The Product Backlog may also be adjusted to meet new opportunities"
Nature "The Sprint Review is a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation"
Place in the Sprint The second to last event
Timebox A maximum of four hours for a one-month Sprint; usually shorter for shorter Sprints

1.2 What is shown and what is not

  • "The sum of the Increments is presented at the Sprint Review thus supporting empiricism."
  • "An Increment may be delivered to stakeholders prior to the end of the Sprint. The Sprint Review should never be considered a gate to releasing value."
  • "If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review. Instead, it returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration."
Exam angle

the Review is a working session with stakeholders that inspects the Increment and adapts the Product Backlog. It is not a demo to approve the Sprint, not a status meeting, and not a release gate. Work that does not meet the Definition of Done is not shown.

1.3 Performing a Sprint Review (CSM 1.9) Beyond the Guide

Step What to do
Before Invite the key stakeholders; check what meets the Definition of Done; the Product Owner knows the state of the Product Backlog and the Product Goal
Open Remind everyone of the purpose, the timebox and the Sprint Goal
Show what is Done The Scrum Team presents the Increment (what meets the Definition of Done), and says what is not Done
Discuss progress Progress toward the Product Goal; what was learned in the Sprint
Inspect the environment What has changed: market, users, technology, constraints
Collaborate Stakeholders and the Scrum Team discuss what to do next; collect feedback
Adjust The Product Owner adjusts the Product Backlog (order, new items, removed items)
Close End within the timebox; next steps are clear. The Retrospective follows
Old wording

The 2017 Guide called it "an informal meeting, not a status meeting", where "the presentation of the Increment is intended to elicit feedback and foster collaboration". It listed attendees invited by the Product Owner, the Product Owner projecting "likely target and delivery dates", a review of "the timeline, budget, potential capabilities, and marketplace", and "the Development Team demonstrates the work". The 2020 Guide is shorter: a working session focusing on the outcome, the environment and what to do next.

2Sprint Retrospective

2.1 Purpose, participants and timebox

Item What the Guide says
Purpose "To plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness"
What the Scrum Team inspects How the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done. Inspected elements often vary with the domain of work
Discussion Assumptions that led them astray are identified and their origins explored. The team discusses what went well, what problems it encountered, and how those problems were (or were not) solved
Output The Scrum Team identifies the most helpful changes to improve its effectiveness. The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible. They may even be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint
Place in the Sprint It concludes the Sprint
Timebox A maximum of three hours for a one-month Sprint; usually shorter for shorter Sprints

The Retrospective is the Scrum Team's event: the whole team, including the Scrum Master and Product Owner, takes part as members. Scrum Alliance's exam study guide gives "only the Scrum Team attends the Retrospective" as an example of something implied by the Guide, not stated.

2.2 Performing a Sprint Retrospective (CSM 1.10) Beyond the Guide

A common structure follows the Guide's content:

Step What to do
1. Set the stage Restate the purpose and the rules; create a safe, open atmosphere (openness, respect, courage)
2. Gather data Look at the Sprint: what happened, what went well, what caused problems (individuals, interactions, processes, tools, the Definition of Done)
3. Generate insights Ask why: which assumptions misled the team and where did they come from?
4. Decide what to do Choose the few most helpful changes, make each one concrete (what, who, how to know it works)
5. Close Add the most impactful improvement to the next Sprint Backlog; check the improvements from the last Retrospective; end within the timebox

Simple formats that fit these steps are only examples: "what went well, what did not, what to change", or "start, stop, continue".

Old wording

The 2017 Guide said the Retrospective "occurs after the Sprint Review and prior to the next Sprint Planning". It said the Scrum Master "participates as a peer team member". The team was to "identify and order the major items that went well and potential improvements" and to plan "ways to increase product quality by improving work processes or adapting the definition of 'Done'".

The 2017 Sprint Backlog also had to include "at least one high priority process improvement". The 2020 Guide says the Retrospective concludes the Sprint, and that improvements "may even be added" to the Sprint Backlog.

3Effects of Skipping the Sprint Retrospective (CSM 1.11)

The objective asks for at least three effects Beyond the Guide, anchored in the Guide's statement that "failure to operate any events as prescribed results in lost opportunities to inspect and adapt."

Effect Explanation
Problems repeat Impediments and mistakes that were not discussed return Sprint after Sprint
No improvement in quality or effectiveness The one event planned for improvement is gone; the team's way of working stagnates
Wrong assumptions stay hidden Assumptions that led the team astray are never examined
Trust and openness erode Without a safe place to speak, concerns and conflicts go unspoken or come out badly
Morale and ownership fall The team feels it cannot influence how it works
The Definition of Done does not improve Quality gaps found in the Sprint are not turned into stronger standards
The Scrum Master cannot improve the team's effectiveness One of the Scrum Master's two accountabilities loses its main tool
Scrum is only partly practised The team is no longer doing Scrum (Topic 1)

4Review and Retrospective Compared

Sprint Review Sprint Retrospective
Inspects The outcome: the Increment and the changing environment The way of working: individuals, interactions, processes, tools, Definition of Done
Adapts The Product Backlog The team's practices; improvements may enter the next Sprint Backlog
Participants The Scrum Team and key stakeholders The Scrum Team
Maximum (one month) 4 hours 3 hours
Position Second to last event Concludes the Sprint
Question What did we build and what should we do next? How did we work and how can we do it better?

5Inspect and Adapt (CSM 1.7)

Event Inspect Example of adaptation Transparency
Sprint Review The Increment and what has changed in the environment The Product Owner reorders the Product Backlog after stakeholder feedback Everyone sees the real state of the product and the Product Goal
Sprint Retrospective How the Sprint went The team adds an improvement, for example a stronger Definition of Done item, to the next Sprint Backlog Problems and their causes are discussed openly

6Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. The Review is a working session, not a presentation, demo-for-approval or status meeting.
  2. The Review is not a gate. An Increment may be delivered before it.
  3. Items that do not meet the Definition of Done are not presented and return to the Product Backlog.
  4. Review: Increment and Product Backlog. Retrospective: people, process, tools and the Definition of Done. Do not mix them.
  5. Review: Scrum Team and key stakeholders. Retrospective: the Scrum Team.
  6. Maximum 4 hours (Review) and 3 hours (Retrospective) for a one-month Sprint.
  7. The Retrospective concludes the Sprint; the Review is second to last. The 2017 wording, "occurs after the Sprint Review and prior to the next Sprint Planning", is old.
  8. The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible and may be added to the next Sprint Backlog.
  9. Skipping the Retrospective loses the planned chance to improve; the best answer restores it and helps the team see its value.
  10. The Scrum Master takes part as a member of the Scrum Team in the Retrospective, and ensures it is positive and productive.
  11. The Product Backlog may be adjusted at the Review, not by the stakeholders alone: the Product Owner decides.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Scrum Team plans a one-hour slide presentation for the Sprint Review and does not expect questions. What should the Scrum Master advise?

  • AMake it a working session where the Scrum Team and stakeholders review what was done and collaborate on next steps
  • BCancel the Review, because a one-way presentation can be replaced by sending the slides to the stakeholders and collecting their written feedback afterwards
  • CAsk the stakeholders to send written feedback after the presentation, so that the Review stays within one hour
  • DAgree, because the Review is a presentation of the Increment to the stakeholders by the Scrum Team
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Sprint Review is a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. Attendees collaborate on what to do next, and the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities.

S2One item is almost done but does not yet meet the Definition of Done. A Developer wants to show it at the Review, "so the stakeholders see progress". What should happen?

  • AShow it and mark it as 90 percent finished, so that the stakeholders can see how far the work has progressed
  • BThe item cannot be presented or released, and returns to the Product Backlog
  • CAsk the stakeholders to approve the item at the Review, so that the Product Owner can accept it as Done
  • DChange the Definition of Done for this item so that it counts as Done, and present it as part of the Increment
Show the answer

Answer: B. If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review. It returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration. Lowering the Definition of Done would undermine transparency.

S3What is the purpose of the Sprint Retrospective?

  • ATo plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness
  • BTo demonstrate the Increment to stakeholders
  • CTo estimate the next Sprint's items
  • DTo report progress to management
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Guide says the purpose is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. Demonstrating the Increment belongs to the Review, and estimating and reporting are not its purposes.

S4The Product Owner says that the Increment may not be given to users until after the Sprint Review. What does the Guide say?

  • AThe Review approves the release, so an Increment may be given to users only after the stakeholders have accepted it at the Sprint Review
  • BOnly the stakeholders may release an Increment, because they are the ones who pay for the product
  • CAn Increment may be delivered before the end of the Sprint, and the Review is never a gate to releasing value
  • DAn Increment must wait for the Retrospective, because the team must first inspect how it was built
Show the answer

Answer: C. The sum of Increments is presented at the Review, but an Increment may be delivered earlier, and the Review is not a gate to releasing value.

S5The Retrospective has produced a long list of ideas. What should the Scrum Team do?

  • AImplement every idea at once, so that none of the improvements that the team has found is lost, delayed or forgotten
  • BChoose the most helpful changes, address the most impactful as soon as possible, and add them to the next Sprint Backlog
  • CKeep the list until the end of the project, when all the improvements can be reviewed and chosen together, with the benefit of everything the team has learned by then
  • DGive the list to the Scrum Master to implement, since the Scrum Master is accountable for the team's effectiveness
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Scrum Team identifies the most helpful changes to improve its effectiveness, the most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible, and they may be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint. The team owns the improvements.

S6A senior manager asks to attend every Sprint Retrospective "to hear what the team's problems are". What is the best response from the Scrum Master?

  • AAgree, since managers should know the problems of the team so that they can support it with the right decisions
  • BAgree, but only if the manager takes notes and shares them with the team after each Retrospective
  • CMake the Retrospective a report to the manager, so that every Developer states what went wrong in the Sprint
  • DExplain that the Retrospective is for the Scrum Team to inspect its own way of working in a safe setting
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Retrospective is the Scrum Team's inspection of how the Sprint went with regard to individuals, interactions, processes, tools and the Definition of Done. Openness and courage need a safe setting. The manager's concerns can be served through the Sprint Review and by the Scrum Master working with the organization.

S7At the Sprint Review a stakeholder suggests a new feature that is more valuable than the next item in the Product Backlog. What should happen?

  • AThe Product Owner considers it with the Scrum Team and stakeholders and may adjust the Product Backlog
  • BThe Developers add it to the Sprint Backlog at once, since the stakeholder has said that it is more valuable
  • CThe Scrum Master adds it to the Product Backlog and orders it above the item that the team planned next
  • DThe stakeholder orders the Product Backlog, because stakeholders know best which items are the most valuable
Show the answer

Answer: A. The attendees collaborate on what to do next, and the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities. The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog's content and order.

S8In which order do the last two events of the Sprint take place?

  • ARetrospective, then Review
  • BReview and Retrospective at the same time
  • CReview (second to last), then Retrospective (concludes the Sprint)
  • DThe Review is held in the next Sprint
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Sprint Review is the second to last event of the Sprint, and the Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint.

S9Which topics does the Guide list for the Scrum Team to inspect in the Retrospective?

  • AOnly the Product Backlog
  • BIndividuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done
  • COnly the Increment
  • DThe performance reviews of the Developers
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools and their Definition of Done. Inspected elements often vary with the domain of work.

S10What is a typical result of a good Sprint Review?

  • AA signed approval of the Sprint by the stakeholders, which confirms that the Developers may start the next Sprint
  • BA list of the hours that each Developer worked in the Sprint, which the Scrum Master reports to management
  • CA decision to extend the Sprint by a few days so that the unfinished items can be completed and shown
  • DAn adjusted Product Backlog and a shared view of what to do next
Show the answer

Answer: D. Attendees collaborate on what to do next, and the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities. The Review is not an approval gate.

7.2 Recall Q&As

R1What is the purpose of the Sprint Review?

Show the answer

To inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.

R2Who attends the Sprint Review?

Show the answer

The Scrum Team and key stakeholders.

R3What is the Sprint Review's nature?

Show the answer

A working session; the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation.

R4Is the Sprint Review a gate to releasing value?

Show the answer

No. An Increment may be delivered before the end of the Sprint.

R5What happens to an item that does not meet the Definition of Done?

Show the answer

It cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review; it returns to the Product Backlog.

R6What is the Sprint Review's timebox?

Show the answer

A maximum of four hours for a one-month Sprint.

R7What is the purpose of the Sprint Retrospective?

Show the answer

To plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.

R8What does the Scrum Team inspect in the Retrospective?

Show the answer

Individuals, interactions, processes, tools and the Definition of Done.

R9What else does the Scrum Team do in the Retrospective?

Show the answer

Identifies assumptions that led them astray and their origins; discusses what went well, what problems it met and how they were or were not solved; identifies the most helpful changes.

R10What happens to the most impactful improvements?

Show the answer

They are addressed as soon as possible and may be added to the next Sprint Backlog.

R11What is the Retrospective's place and timebox?

Show the answer

It concludes the Sprint; a maximum of three hours for a one-month Sprint.

R12Name at least three effects of skipping the Retrospective.

Show the answer

Problems repeat; no improvement in quality or effectiveness; wrong assumptions stay hidden; trust and openness erode; morale falls; the Definition of Done does not improve.

R13What does the Guide say about skipping any event?

Show the answer

Failure to operate any events as prescribed results in lost opportunities to inspect and adapt.

R14How did the 2017 Guide describe the Review?

Show the answer

As an informal meeting, not a status meeting, held to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Review Retrospective
Purpose Inspect the outcome of the Sprint; determine future adaptations Plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness
Inspects Increment and the environment Individuals, interactions, processes, tools, Definition of Done
Participants Scrum Team and key stakeholders Scrum Team
Adapts Product Backlog Practices; improvements may enter the next Sprint Backlog
Timebox (1-month Sprint) 4 hours 3 hours
Position Second to last Concludes the Sprint
Nature Working session, never a gate Honest, safe, leads to action
Not Done Cannot be presented; back to the Product Backlog The Definition of Done itself may be improved
Skipping Lose stakeholder inspection Problems repeat, no improvement, trust erodes
Old wording "Informal meeting", target dates (2017) after the Review and before Planning, "peer team member" (2017)
